records.source: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הָל֛וֹךְ וְקָנִ֥יתָ בַקְבֻּ֖ק יוֹצֵ֣ר חָ֑רֶשׂ וּמִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וּמִזִּקְנֵ֖י הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃
records.gloss: Thus said Yahweh: go and buy [a] flask of [a] potter, earthenware, and from [the] elders of the people and from [the] elders of the priests,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said this: "Go and buy a clay flask from a potter. Take with you some of the elders of the people and some of the senior priests,

L.1: Thus said {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "Go and buy a potter's earthenware flask, and [take] some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests,

R.1: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said: "Go and buy a clay jar from a potter. Then take some of the leaders of the people and some of the leading priests with you.

decisions.choice: flask: a narrow-necked clay jar of fired earthenware
decisions.reason: The word names a jar with a narrow neck, used for water or other liquids, perhaps named for the gurgling sound it makes when poured. It was fired clay, so once broken it could not be mended (19:11). The word is close in sound to the verb "empty out" in 19:7, a play on words the sign depends on.

decisions.choice: and some of the elders of the people and of the elders of the priests: the verb "take" is understood
decisions.reason: The sentence names the men without a verb; the sense "take some of them with you" is clear from 19:10, where they go with Jeremiah. The Greek translation supplies "take".

decisions.choice: Thus said the LORD: with no "to me"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name the hearer here; the Greek translation adds "to me". The command is plainly to Jeremiah, as in 13:1, where the Hebrew has "to me". This claim about the Greek is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: the elders of the priests: the leading, senior priests
decisions.reason: The elders of the people were the heads of families who spoke for the city. The elders of the priests were the senior members of the priesthood (2 Kings 19:2). Both groups are witnesses to the sign.

decisions.choice: [take]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the verb that the sentence leaves understood.

decisions.choice: senior priests (B); leading priests (R)
decisions.reason: "Elders of the priests" would suggest old age; Balanced and Readable say what the title meant. Readable says "leaders of the people" for the elders of the people, and starts a new sentence.

records.heading: Jeremiah breaks a flask

records.source: וְיָצָ֨אתָ֙ אֶל־גֵּ֣יא בֶן־הִנֹּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֕ר פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הַֽחַרְסִ֑ית וְקָרָ֣אתָ שָּׁ֔ם אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: and go out to [the] valley of Ben-hinnom which [is at the] entrance of [the] gate of the Harsith, and proclaim there the words that I will speak to you.
pieces: and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, by the entrance of the Potsherd Gate. There proclaim the words I tell you.

L.2: and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, which [is at] the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words that I will speak to you.

R.2: Go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, near the entrance to the Gate of Broken Pots. There announce the message I give you.

decisions.choice: the Potsherd Gate: a gate of Jerusalem opening onto the Valley of Ben-hinnom, probably named for broken pottery
alternatives: the Harsith Gate (left as a name)
decisions.reason: The name is found only here. It seems to come from the word for a piece of broken pottery, so it may have been the gate where potters worked or where broken pots were thrown out into the valley. That would suit a sign with a clay flask. Some identify it with the Dung Gate of Nehemiah 2:13, which also led to this valley, but that is not certain.

decisions.choice: Harsith: the reading the Hebrew margin gives
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a slightly different spelling of the gate's name; the margin's reading is followed. The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Ben-hinnom: the valley of Topheth (7:31; 2 Kings 23:10)
decisions.reason: The valley below the south side of Jerusalem, where Topheth was. The name is given as in 7:31 and 2 Kings 23:10.

decisions.choice: the Gate of Broken Pots
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gate's name probably means, since "potsherd" is not an everyday word. The decision on the name says why it is uncertain.

records.source: וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֔ה מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֖י יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא רָעָה֙ עַל־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּל־שֹׁמְעָ֖הּ תִּצַּ֥לְנָה אָזְנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And say: hear [the] word of Yahweh, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: look, I [am] bringing disaster on the place this, which everyone hearing it, will tingle his ears.
pieces: Say: 'Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Look, I am about to bring such disaster on this place that it will make the ears of all who hear of it tingle,

L.3: And say, 'Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing disaster on this place, at which the ears of everyone who hears it will tingle,

R.3: Say to them: 'Listen to the message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you kings of Judah and you people who live in Jerusalem. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring a disaster on this place that is so shocking that it will make the ears of everyone who hears about it ring.

decisions.choice: the ears of everyone who hears it will tingle: news so terrible that it stuns all who hear it
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of the judgment on Eli's house (1 Samuel 3:11) and of the disaster announced for Manasseh's sins (2 Kings 21:12). Jeremiah takes up the words of 2 Kings 21:12 almost exactly, for the judgment that was announced then is now coming.

decisions.choice: I am bringing disaster on this place: the wording of 2 Kings 21:12 and 22:16
decisions.reason: The prophecies under Manasseh and Josiah announced disaster on "this place", Jerusalem. The wording here is given as in 2 Kings 21:12, with "this place" for "Jerusalem and Judah" and "his ears" for "both his ears".

decisions.choice: kings of Judah: the king and the royal house
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks to the kings in the plural, as in 17:20: the reigning king and the house of David with him, who are responsible for the city's worship.

decisions.choice: people of Jerusalem (B); people who live in Jerusalem (R)
decisions.reason: "Inhabitants" means everyone who lives in the city; Balanced and Readable say it in everyday words.

decisions.choice: so shocking that it will make the ears ... ring
decisions.reason: As 1 Samuel 3:11 and 2 Kings 21:12, Readable says why the ears ring and leaves out "look", since "Listen" opens the speech.

records.source: יַ֣עַן׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲזָבֻ֗נִי וַֽיְנַכְּר֞וּ אֶת־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ וַיְקַטְּרוּ־בוֹ֙ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יְדָע֛וּם הֵ֥מָּה וַאֲבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם וּמַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וּמָֽלְא֛וּ אֶת־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה דַּ֥ם נְקִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: Because that they have forsaken me and have made foreign the place this, and they have burned incense in it to gods other whom not they knew them, they and their fathers and [the] kings of Judah; and they have filled the place this [with] blood of innocent [ones].
pieces: because they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and made this place belong to foreign gods. They have burned incense in it to other gods, gods that neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah had ever known, and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocent.

L.4: because they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and have made this place foreign, and have burned incense in it to other gods whom they had not known, they and their fathers and the kings of Judah; and they have filled this place [with] the blood of innocents.

R.4: I will do this because they have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They have made this place a home for foreign gods. They have burned incense here to other gods that they, their ancestors and the kings of Judah never knew. They have filled this place with the blood of innocent people.

decisions.choice: made this place foreign: handed over the city or its sacred place to strange gods, so that it no longer belonged to the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat something as foreign or strange. Here it means they have made the LORD's place a place of foreign worship, as the rest of the verse explains. "This place" may mean Jerusalem as a whole or the valley where Jeremiah stands.

decisions.choice: they and their fathers and the kings of Judah: the ones who had never known these gods
decisions.reason: The three groups go with "whom they had not known": these gods were new, with no history with the people and no claim on them (Deuteronomy 32:17).

decisions.choice: the blood of innocents: innocent people killed, above all the children sacrificed in the valley
alternatives: innocent people murdered in the city
decisions.reason: The next verse speaks of the children burned there, and that is the first sense. The words also recall the innocent blood Manasseh shed through Jerusalem (2 Kings 21:16; 24:4).

decisions.choice: burned incense: made offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb is used for burning incense and also for burning offerings on an altar. Either way it is worship given to other gods.

decisions.choice: made this place belong to foreign gods (B); made this place a home for foreign gods (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "made foreign" means here, drawing on the rest of the verse.

decisions.choice: I will do this
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and says what the reason is for.

records.source: וּבָנ֞וּ אֶת־בָּמ֣וֹת הַבַּ֗עַל לִשְׂרֹ֧ף אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֛ם בָּאֵ֖שׁ עֹל֣וֹת לַבָּ֑עַל אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־צִוִּ֨יתִי֙ וְלֹ֣א דִבַּ֔רְתִּי וְלֹ֥א עָלְתָ֖ה עַל־לִבִּֽי׃פ
records.gloss: And they have built [the] high places of the Baal to burn their sons in the fire [as] burnt offerings to the Baal, which not I commanded and not I spoke and not it came up on my heart.
pieces: They have built Baal's high places to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal, a thing I never commanded or spoke of, and that never entered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind.

L.5: And they have built the high places of Baal, to burn their sons in the fire [as] burnt offerings to Baal, which I did not command and did not speak, and [which] did not come up into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart.

R.5: They have built shrines for Baal, and there they burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal. I never commanded that or spoke of it. I never even thought of such a thing.

decisions.choice: which I did not command, nor speak, nor did it come into my mind: as 7:31, with "nor speak" added
decisions.reason: The same words close 7:31, and 32:35 repeats them of Molech. Here a third denial is added: God never gave such an order, never spoke of it, never even thought of it. The wording is given as in 7:31 at each level.

decisions.choice: to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal: child sacrifice offered as worship
decisions.reason: The "burnt offering" was the offering wholly burned on the altar. To burn children in the same way was what the Law forbade as something God hates (Deuteronomy 12:31; 18:10). 7:31 speaks of the same practice at Topheth, and 32:35 links it with Molech; here it is offered to Baal.

decisions.choice: the high places of Baal: raised places of worship built for Baal in the valley
decisions.reason: As in 7:31, the high places here are platforms or altars built in the valley, not hilltop shrines.

decisions.choice: their sons: their children, with sons named as the usual victims
decisions.reason: The word can mean sons or children in general; 7:31 speaks of sons and daughters.

decisions.choice: shrines
decisions.reason: As 7:31, Readable says "shrines" for the high places in the valley.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה־יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹא־יִקָּרֵא֩ לַמָּק֨וֹם הַזֶּ֥ה ע֛וֹד הַתֹּ֖פֶת וְגֵ֣יא בֶן־הִנֹּ֑ם כִּ֖י אִם־גֵּ֥יא הַהֲרֵגָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore look, days [are] coming, declaration of Yahweh, and not it will be called to the place this again the Topheth and [the] valley of Ben-hinnom, but [the] valley of the slaughter.
pieces: So look, the days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when people will no longer call this place Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom; they will call it the Valley of Slaughter.

L.6: Therefore look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

R.6: So the time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when people will no longer call this place Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom. They will call it the Valley of Slaughter.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Slaughter: as 7:32
decisions.reason: The words repeat 7:32, with "this place" named. The wording follows 7:32 at each level, except that Balanced, like Readable, says "people will no longer call this place" for "this place will no longer be called". The place where they killed their children will be filled with their own dead.

decisions.choice: days are coming: a time is coming
decisions.reason: As in 7:32.

decisions.choice: the time is coming
people will no longer call this place
alternatives: this place will no longer be called
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the passive "will no longer be called" into an active verb with "people" as its subject; the sense is the same.

records.source: וּ֠בַקֹּתִי אֶת־עֲצַ֨ת יְהוּדָ֤ה וִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ בַּמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִפַּלְתִּ֤ים בַּחֶ֨רֶב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְיַ֖ד מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת־נִבְלָתָם֙ לְמַֽאֲכָ֔ל לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְבֶהֱמַ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I will empty out [the] plan of Judah and Jerusalem in the place this, and I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies and by [the] hand of [those] seeking their life; and I will give their corpses as food to [the] birds of the heavens and to [the] beasts of the earth.
pieces: In this place I will empty out the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will have them cut down by the sword in front of their enemies, by the hand of those who want to kill them, and I will give their dead bodies as food to the birds of the sky and the wild animals.

L.7: And I will empty out the plan of Judah and Jerusalem in this place, and I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies and by the hand of those who seek their life; and I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the heavens and to the beasts of the earth.

R.7: In this place I will pour out the plans of Judah and Jerusalem like water from a jar, and they will come to nothing. I will let their enemies kill them with the sword, the enemies who want them dead. I will give their dead bodies to the birds and wild animals to eat.

decisions.choice: I will empty out the plan: make their plans come to nothing, like a flask poured out
alternatives: I will make void the plan
I will pour out the plan
decisions.reason: The verb means to empty or lay waste, and it sounds like the word for the flask Jeremiah carries (19:1). The flask may have been poured out as he spoke; the text says only that it was broken (19:10). Either way the sound ties the word to the sign: as the flask is emptied, so the plans of Judah and Jerusalem, their schemes for safety and their trust in other gods, will be emptied of all their force.

decisions.choice: those who seek their life: those who want to kill them
decisions.reason: To seek someone's life means to seek to kill them (11:21; 1 Kings 19:10).

decisions.choice: their corpses as food for the birds and the beasts: the covenant curse of Deuteronomy 28:26
decisions.reason: As 7:33, the words recall the curse in Deuteronomy 28:26. To lie unburied was the deepest disgrace.

decisions.choice: pour out ... like water from a jar, and they will come to nothing
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture behind the verb so that the link with the jar of 19:1 can be seen; the jar is not named in the Hebrew of this verse.

decisions.choice: the birds of the sky and the wild animals (B); the birds and wild animals (R)

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּי֙ אֶת־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את לְשַׁמָּ֖ה וְלִשְׁרֵקָ֑ה כֹּ֚ל עֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק עַל־כָּל־מַכֹּתֶֽהָ׃
records.gloss: And I will make the city this into a horror and into a hissing; everyone passing by it will be appalled and will hiss over all its blows.
pieces: I will make this city a horror and an object of scorn. Everyone who passes by will be appalled and will hiss in scorn at all its wounds.

L.8: And I will make this city a horror and a hissing; everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will hiss over all its blows.

R.8: I will make this city a horror, something people mock. Everyone who passes by will be shocked and will make fun of it because of all the disasters that have struck it.

decisions.choice: a hissing; will hiss: the sound people made at a sight of ruin, in scorn and in shock
decisions.reason: The hissing or whistling of passers-by was a gesture of horror and of mockery at a ruined place (18:16; 1 Kings 9:8; Lamentations 2:15). The city will become a byword for disaster.

decisions.choice: a horror; will be appalled: a desolation that stuns those who see it
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb come from one root, which means both to be laid waste and to be stunned with horror. The ruin and the shock it causes go together.

decisions.choice: all its blows: the wounds the city has suffered
decisions.reason: The word means a blow or a wound, and so a disaster that strikes. The city is pictured as a body covered with wounds.

decisions.choice: an object of scorn; hiss in scorn (B); something people mock; make fun of (R)
decisions.reason: As the book's list "horror, hissing, curse", Balanced and Readable say what the hissing meant.

records.source: וְהַֽאֲכַלְתִּ֞ים אֶת־בְּשַׂ֣ר בְּנֵיהֶ֗ם וְאֵת֙ בְּשַׂ֣ר בְּנֹתֵיהֶ֔ם וְאִ֥ישׁ בְּשַׂר־רֵעֵ֖הוּ יֹאכֵ֑לוּ בְּמָצוֹר֙ וּבְמָצ֔וֹק אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצִ֧יקוּ לָהֶ֛ם אֹיְבֵיהֶ֖ם וּמְבַקְשֵׁ֥י נַפְשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And I will make them eat [the] flesh of their sons and [the] flesh of their daughters, and each [the] flesh of his neighbor they will eat, in [the] siege and in [the] distress with which will distress them their enemies and [those] seeking their life.
pieces: I will make them eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters, and they will eat each other's flesh during the siege, in the distress that their enemies and those who want to kill them bring upon them.'

L.9: And I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and each will eat the flesh of {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, in the siege and in the distress with which their enemies and those who seek their life will distress them.'

R.9: Their enemies, who want them dead, will surround the city and trap them inside. In that desperate time I will make them eat their own sons and daughters, and they will eat one another.'

decisions.choice: eating the flesh of sons and daughters in the siege and distress: the covenant curse of Deuteronomy 28:53
decisions.reason: The words take up Deuteronomy 28:53, "in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you", one of the curses for breaking the covenant. The wording is given as in Deuteronomy 28:53. Lamentations 2:20 and 4:10 tell that it came true when Jerusalem fell.

decisions.choice: the siege and the distress: a city shut in by an army until its food runs out
decisions.reason: In a long siege no food could come in, and people starved. The two words, which sound alike, stress the pressure and the hopelessness.

decisions.choice: I will make them eat: God lets the curse fall on them
decisions.reason: The verb is causative: God is the one who brings them to this. It does not mean he wants the deed, but that the judgment he warned of in the covenant will come.

decisions.choice: the end of Jeremiah's message to the kings and people
decisions.reason: The words Jeremiah was told to say, begun in 19:3, end here. 19:10 returns to God's instructions to Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: Their enemies ... will surround the city and trap them inside. Then
decisions.reason: Readable puts the siege first and says what a siege is, so that the order of events is clear.

decisions.choice: each other's flesh (B); eat one another (R)
decisions.reason: "Each the flesh of his neighbor" means that the starving people eat each other; Balanced and Readable say it without a pronoun.

records.source: וְשָׁבַרְתָּ֖ הַבַּקְבֻּ֑ק לְעֵינֵי֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַהֹלְכִ֖ים אוֹתָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And break the flask before [the] eyes of the men going with you.
pieces: Then break the flask while the men who went with you watch,

L.10: And break the flask before the eyes of the men who go with you,

R.10: Then break the jar while the men who went with you are watching.

decisions.choice: break the flask: a sign acted out before witnesses
decisions.reason: The breaking is the message made visible, as in 13:1-11. The men who go with Jeremiah, the elders of 19:1, will see it and can bear witness to what was said.

decisions.choice: comma at the end
decisions.reason: The command runs on into 19:11, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר׀יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת כָּ֣כָה אֶשְׁבֹּ֞ר אֶת־הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְאֶת־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁבֹּר֙ אֶת־כְּלִ֣י הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־יוּכַ֥ל לְהֵרָפֵ֖ה ע֑וֹד וּבְתֹ֣פֶת יִקְבְּר֔וּ מֵאֵ֥ין מָק֖וֹם לִקְבּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And say to them: thus says Yahweh of hosts: thus I will break the people this and the city this, as that one breaks the vessel of the potter which not it can be mended again; and in Topheth they will bury from there is not place to bury.
pieces: and say to them: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: In the same way I will break this people and this city, as a potter's jar is broken that can never be mended. They will bury the dead in Topheth because there will be no other place left to bury them.

L.11: and say to them, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: So I will break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter's vessel, which cannot be mended again; and they will bury in Topheth because there is no place [else] to bury.

R.11: Say to them: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: I will smash this people and this city, just as someone smashes a clay pot that can never be put back together. They will bury the dead in Topheth because there will be no room left anywhere else.

decisions.choice: as a potter's vessel that cannot be mended: a judgment that cannot be undone
decisions.reason: In 18:1-11 the clay was still soft and the potter could rework it, and the people were called to turn back. Here the vessel is fired clay, and once smashed it cannot be repaired. The time for reshaping has passed.

decisions.choice: because there is no place to bury: for lack of space elsewhere
alternatives: until there is no place left to bury
decisions.reason: As in 7:32, where the words are discussed. The dead will be buried even in the unclean ground of Topheth because no other ground is left.

decisions.choice: they will bury in Topheth: as 7:32
decisions.reason: The words repeat 7:32, with "to bury" added at the end. The wording is given as in 7:32.

decisions.choice: smash
decisions.reason: Readable says "smash", since breaking clay pottery means smashing it to pieces.

records.source: כֵּֽן־אֶעֱשֶׂ֞ה לַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה וּלְיֽוֹשְׁבָ֑יו וְלָתֵ֛ת אֶת־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את כְּתֹֽפֶת׃
records.gloss: Thus I will do to the place this, declaration of Yahweh, and to its inhabitants, and to make the city this like Topheth.
pieces: This is what I will do to this place and to the people who live here, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: I will make this city like Topheth.

L.12: Thus I will do to this place, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to its inhabitants, making this city like Topheth.

R.12: This is what I will do to this place and to the people who live here, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will make this city like Topheth.

decisions.choice: to make this city like Topheth: Jerusalem will become a place of the dead and unclean, like the valley
decisions.reason: Topheth was the place of their child sacrifices, made unclean by Josiah (2 Kings 23:10) and filled with graves (19:11). The whole city will share its fate: what they did there will be done to them.

decisions.choice: declares (B); says (R) the LORD moved
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move "declares the LORD" so the list of those affected stays together.

records.source: וְהָי֞וּ בָּתֵּ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם וּבָתֵּי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה כִּמְק֥וֹם הַתֹּ֖פֶת הַטְּמֵאִ֑ים לְכֹ֣ל הַבָּתִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר קִטְּר֜וּ עַל־גַּגֹּֽתֵיהֶם֙ לְכֹל֙ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְהַסֵּ֥ךְ נְסָכִ֖ים לֵאלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And will be [the] houses of Jerusalem and [the] houses of [the] kings of Judah like [the] place of the Topheth, the unclean [ones], all the houses which they burned incense on their roofs to all [the] host of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to gods other.
pieces: The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of Judah's kings will be unclean like the place of Topheth: all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to the whole host of heaven, and poured drink offerings out to other gods.'"

L.13: And the houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be like the place of Topheth, unclean, all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to other gods.'"

R.13: The houses in Jerusalem and the palaces of the kings of Judah will become unclean like Topheth. On the roofs of all those houses they burned incense to the stars in the sky and poured out drink offerings to other gods.'"

decisions.choice: on whose roofs they burned incense to the host of heaven: worship of the sun, moon and stars on flat rooftops
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs, open to the sky, where people could worship the stars and planets (32:29; Zephaniah 1:5). Josiah had pulled down such rooftop altars (2 Kings 23:12), but the practice had returned.

decisions.choice: unclean: describing the houses, made unclean like Topheth
alternatives: like the place of Topheth, which is unclean
decisions.reason: The word stands after "like the place of Topheth" and describes the houses: they will be defiled as Topheth was, by the dead and by their own idolatry.

decisions.choice: the host of heaven: the stars and other heavenly bodies worshiped as gods
decisions.reason: As 8:2 and 2 Kings 23:5, the "host" or army of the heavens means the sun, moon and stars, worshiped as powers.

decisions.choice: God's instructions to Jeremiah, begun in 19:1, and his message for the people, begun in 19:11, end here
decisions.reason: 19:14 returns to the story told about Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: palaces; the stars in the sky
decisions.reason: Readable says "palaces" for the houses of the kings and "the stars in the sky" for the host of heaven, as 2 Kings 23:5 does.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵֽהַתֹּ֔פֶת אֲשֶׁ֨ר שְׁלָח֧וֹ יְהוָ֛ה שָׁ֖ם לְהִנָּבֵ֑א וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר בֵּית־יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֶל־כָּל־הָעָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And came Jeremiah from the Topheth, where had sent him Yahweh there to prophesy, and he stood in [the] court of [the] house of Yahweh and said to all the people:
pieces: Then Jeremiah came back from Topheth, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sent him to prophesy. He took his stand in the court of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house and spoke to all the people:

L.14: And Jeremiah came from Topheth, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said to all the people,

R.14: Then Jeremiah came back from Topheth, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sent him to give his message. He stood in the courtyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and said to all the people there,

decisions.choice: Jeremiah came: the account now speaks of Jeremiah in the third person
decisions.reason: 19:1-13 gave God's instructions to Jeremiah; this verse tells what he did. The report of the sign itself in the valley is left out; it is assumed that he did as he was told.

decisions.choice: the court of the LORD's house: the open courtyard of the temple, where the people gathered
decisions.reason: From the valley Jeremiah went up into the city to the temple court, so that his message reached all the people, not only the elders. His preaching there leads to his arrest in 20:1-2.

decisions.choice: came back
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had gone out to the valley at God's command (19:2); Balanced and Readable say he returned.

decisions.choice: to give his message; temple
decisions.reason: Readable says what prophesying was here, and "temple" for the LORD's house, as 7:2 does.

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֜יא אֶל־הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ וְעַל־כָּל־עָרֶ֔יהָ אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּ֤י הִקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־עָרְפָּ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמ֥וֹעַ אֶת־דְּבָרָֽי׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: look, I [am] bringing to the city this and upon all its towns all the disaster which I have spoken against it, because they have hardened their neck so as not to hear my words.
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Look, I am about to bring on this city and all its towns all the disaster I have announced against it, because they have stiffened their necks and refused to listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words."

L.15: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing on this city and on all its towns all the disaster that I have spoken against it, because they have stiffened their neck so as not to hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words."

R.15: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring every disaster I said would come on this city and on all the towns around it. I will do this because they have been stubborn and refused to listen to what I said."

decisions.choice: they have stiffened their neck: they have stubbornly refused to obey
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox that will not bend its neck to the yoke (7:26; 17:23; Deuteronomy 10:16).

decisions.choice: all its towns: the towns of Judah that belonged to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem is pictured as the mother city with its towns around it; the judgment will reach the whole land.

decisions.choice: I am bringing: the reading the Hebrew margin gives
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text spells the verb without its last letter; the margin's fuller spelling is followed. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: they have been stubborn
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the stiff neck means.
